column4: The histories of towns include some still standing and others reaped flat, an unusually exact Quranic pairing of upright trace and leveled remnant.
Abraham asks whether his people worship what they carve, carrying the mountain-house verb نحت into the setting of fashioned cult objects.
After the question about human carving in 37:95, Abraham says God created both them and what they make, subordinating craft to creation.
Pharaoh's people are made a precedent and a مثل for later peoples, turning the section's “likeness” word into the exemplary afterlife of a destroyed civilization.
God destroyed generations stronger in might who ranged through the lands seeking escape, directly answering monumental confidence in power and place.
A town's affluent people rebel and it is utterly destroyed, joining material elevation, boundary-breaking and civilizational collapse.
Many wrongdoing towns are shattered and replaced by other peoples, a direct city-scale counterpart to breaking a wall or mountain.
The shattered people of 21:11 are made like reaped growth and extinguished, specifying their movement from standing life to flattened residue.
The earth is made a resting spread immediately before mountains are named as pegs in 78:7, completing the section's paired ground-and-stake image.
God spreads the earth before 79:32 describes anchoring its mountains, joining prepared ground to fixed height in one creation sequence.
God makes earth a bed and sky a built canopy, placing level ground and unsupported divine architecture together.
God makes earth a settled place, sky a structure and human forms beautiful, uniting ground, building and measured creation under one maker.
People are asked to look at the sky God built above them without fissures, contrasting the flawless cosmic structure with vulnerable human monuments.
God sets firm mountains above earth and measures its sustenance, bringing stabilizing heights and apportioned provision into the same creation scene.
The sky is made a protected roof, another divine form of shelter whose security does not depend on a visible human column.
The trust is offered to heavens, earth and mountains, which refuse to bear it, making the section's load-bearing image morally explicit.
A mountain would humble itself and split from fear of God if made to bear the Quran, showing the hardest height lowered and fractured by divine weight.
David is commanded to make full coats of armor and measure their links precisely, a Quranic craft scene close to the section's measuring before cutting.
The question “is one who creates like one who does not create?” places خلق and likeness-comparison together while drawing the creator-created boundary.
The worshiper's declaration “You alone we serve” supplies the عبد side of the path requested in the following ayah.
The request for guidance to the straight path follows worship in 1:5, explicitly meeting the section's servant and trodden-road senses.
Jinn and humans are created to worship God, joining خلق directly to the عبد destination with which the section ends.
God has made a measure for everything, extending the section's crafted proportion beyond buildings and provision into a universal rule.
Every thing is held in divine stores and sent down only in known measure, a precise parallel to making and provisioning by proportion.
God says He has honored all children of Adam, locating human dignity in divine gift rather than abundance, height or monumental power.
The question whether wealth and sons are being hurried to people as benefits exposes the same mistaken reading of material increase as favor.
The answer to 23:55 is that they do not perceive, explicitly rejecting prosperity as a transparent measure of divine honor.
Every soul dies and is tested with both adversity and good before returning, supplying the governing frame for the two material trials in surah 89.
The person who طغى is singled out, repeating the section's movement from a named tyrant to the general human act of crossing limits.
Preferring the nearer life is the concrete orientation paired with transgression in 79:37, explaining what the overreacher raises above the lasting end.
A person's wealth does not benefit him when he falls, compressing amassed property, imagined security and downward collapse into one question.
On the Day people are called to prostrate but cannot, showing the boundary between chosen lowering in life and forced incapacity at judgment.
Their eyes are humbled and humiliation covers them because they had refused prostration while able, joining imposed abasement to rejected voluntary descent.
Faces are humbled before the Living Sustainer and the bearer of wrongdoing fails, staging universal human lowering on the judgment ground.
A heart can remain مطمئن in faith under outward coercion, separating inward tranquility from status, safety or visible ease.
God permits certain houses to be raised so His name is remembered in them, giving elevated building a worshipful purpose opposite Aad's playful monuments.
Abraham and Ishmael raise the House's foundations while asking God to accept their work, contrasting prayerful construction with architecture meant to immortalize its makers.
After identifying what God created, the ayah asks what others have created, drawing a sharp boundary between divine creation and human claims.
Good speech rises to God and righteous action raises it, locating true ascent in word and deed rather than physical height.
Lofty chambers built above other chambers are promised by God to the mindful, presenting enduring height as gift rather than a tyrant's self-made claim.
Iron is softened for David immediately before he is told to measure armor links, setting up the contrast between hard material and fine workmanship.
God teaches David the craft of armor for human protection, treating skilled manufacture as taught service rather than autonomous greatness.
A wall about to collapse is restored, a literal scene of failing structure repaired for a merciful purpose hidden beneath it.
Abraham questions his people's devotion to تماثيل, carrying the section's likeness root into standing fashioned representations.
Abraham reduces the statues of 21:52 to fragments, a small-scale enactment of erected human forms being broken down.
Even a mustard seed enclosed inside a rock is brought forth by God, setting divine access against the apparent impenetrability of hard stone.
God spreads earth and places firm mountains in it, another creation formula pairing horizontal habitation with stable height.
Earth is spread and firm mountains cast upon it, repeating the divine arrangement that judgment later dismantles.
Earth is extended and firm mountains set in it, another direct formulation of level expanse and anchored elevation.
God spreads earth and calls Himself an excellent spreader, providing a creation-side counterpart to eschatological leveling.
The oath by the raised roof most naturally evokes heaven as an elevated canopy, reinforcing the section's divine-building counterimage.
Seven layered heavens show no disparity in the Merciful's creation, making faultless proportion the mark of divine workmanship.
Creator, originator and fashioner occur together among God's names, distinguishing initiating and forming from the city's claim to novelty.
Successive bodily formation culminates in “another creation” and praise of the best of creators, moving the craft vocabulary into living form.
The question whether humans were created from nothing or are themselves creators challenges self-grounded existence beneath every human work.
The next question asks whether they created heavens and earth, scaling the challenge in 52:35 up to cosmic construction.
Earlier generations were more firmly established, supplied with rain and rivers, yet destroyed for their sins, another material-strength reversal.
Whole generations disappear until neither a person nor even a whisper is sensed, closely matching the section's erased-trace detail.
People dwell in the homes of former wrongdoers after their fate has become clear, turning ruined habitation into a visible warning.
Past peoples are each given explanatory examples and then utterly destroyed, joining مثل as lesson to the fate of human powers.
Pharaoh's people leave behind many gardens and springs, beginning a catalog of the settled world abandoned after his fall.
Crops and noble stations are also left behind, adding cultivated and prestigious places to the ruler's vanished height.
The comforts in which Pharaoh's people delighted are abandoned, completing the reversal from possessed grandeur to empty trace.
Pharaoh's magicians are told to come in a single صف, a human display-row that will shortly collapse into their voluntary prostration.
The believer is told to lower the wing of humility to parents, offering a deliberate bodily metaphor for gentle descent.
The Prophet is told to lower his wing to believers, another chosen lowering set against tyrannical self-elevation.
The command to lower one's wing to believing followers repeats humility as a deliberate posture.
Divine aid is made good news so hearts may become reassured, locating tranquility in trust rather than monuments or provision.
The same reassurance formula makes victory only a means for hearts to rest, while help itself remains from God.
Abraham asks to see revival so his heart may become reassured, connecting inward tranquility to witnessed re-creation after disassembly.
God constricts and expands and to Him people return, placing material limitation and abundance within return rather than personal worth.
God expands provision for whom He wills and constrains it, repeating the precise theological correction to “my Lord humiliated me.”
Expansion and constraint of provision are called a sign, warning against reading either condition as a simple verdict on dignity.
God expands and constrains provision and replaces what people spend, connecting measured sustenance to responsible use.
The repeated expansion-and-constraint formula is again made a sign for believers rather than an index of rank.
Wealth and children are explicitly called a trial, clarifying why abundance in surah 89 cannot by itself mean honor.
Wealth and children are again named as a test, a repeated boundary on the prosperity judgment made by the human speaker.
People prefer the nearer life, naming the temporal choice beneath attempts to build or possess as though they would remain.
The hereafter is better and more lasting, supplying the true permanence against the preference stated in 87:16.
Muhammad says he is no unprecedented novelty among messengers; this secondary sense of “without precedent” faintly clarifies what a claim of unmatched newness does and does not mean.
